title: Chicken thigh, fried, coated, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken thigh, deep‑fried in a breaded coating, served in fast‑food outlets without the edible skin. The thigh meat is flavorful and the crispy crust adds a pleasant texture. This item is commonly found in burgers, combo meals and other quick‑service dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken thighs contain more fat than breast meat, making them juicier when fried.
The coating is usually a mixture of flour, spices and sometimes breadcrumbs, giving it a golden color.
Many fast‑food chains use proprietary spice blends that include paprika, garlic and onion powder.
Chicken is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide.
Deep‑frying is typically done at 175‑180 °C (350‑360 °F) to create a quick crust while limiting oil absorption.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken thigh provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains niacin (B3) and pyridoxine (B6), which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals are important for immune health and blood formation.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The fat in the thigh offers a quick source of energy, useful for active lifestyles.

items.title: Provides selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant and supports thyroid function.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Fried, breaded meat can contribute to weight gain if consumed frequently.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Salt and seasoning in the coating raise sodium levels, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: If partially hydrogenated oil is used, trans fats may be present, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Allergy to coating ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to wheat, eggs or dairy components in the breading.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Breaded chicken thigh is easy to eat with your hands as part of a burger, in a combo with fries, or sliced into a salad. The skin is usually removed before consumption. Pair it with yogurt‑based, tomato or mustard sauces for added flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked product in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C, where it remains good for up to 3 months. Reheat until the internal temperature reaches 75 °C (165 °F) to ensure safety.
